- Primary compliance drivers: SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA for a subset of customers, and GDPR commitments for EU-subject data.
- Data residency preference: US-only for initial scope; evaluating EU region later.

Action items (owner, ETA):
1) FinSight -> share current list of required evidence and any existing BAA language (Jamie) — target: 10/05
2) FinSight -> provide the initial subprocessor/third-party roster you have internally (Jamie) — target: 10/05
3) Redwood -> share our canonical subprocessor roster + SOC 2 Type II report (Aditya) — I attached the current SOC2 PDF and a CSV roster stub to this thread.
4) Redwood Security -> confirm whether any telemetry/analytics vendors or support tooling may access plaintext payloads and provide controls (Sean) — target: 10/06

Immediate ask: can you confirm if a BAA is required for the initial pilot, or only for production handling PHI? That will inform how we scope the BAA + encryption controls.

Thanks — looping in a couple of technical notes and the current subprocessor export. Attaching redwood_subprocessors_20261003.csv and a short notes doc. Below are the highlights so FinSight has quick answers: 

High-level subprocessor summary (current):
- Core compute & storage: AWS (us-west-2) — model serving and primary storage (S3).
- Backup replication: GCP (us-east1) — snapshot replication for DR only; no live serving in EU.
- Observability: Datadog (metrics/traces), logs forwarded to a retained, encrypted S3 bucket — we can set retention and obfuscation rules per-customer on Dedicated/Private plans.
- Error reporting/issue tracking: Sentry (only stack frames and metadata; we can opt-out of payload capture).
- Monitoring & alerting: PagerDuty (no data access beyond alert metadata).

On the PHI/BAA question: we have an established BAA flow and legal template; we'll engage our Legal to prepare an initial BAA once the scope is confirmed. For the pilot we can proceed with scoping language that excludes PHI until BAA is executed.

Region locking: for Dedicated customers we support strict region isolation. For Hosted customers, we offer region selection and will not replicate customer data to other regions unless explicitly configured. For your stated requirement (US-only), we can enforce US region routing for the pilot.

Logging and prompt telemetry: default behavior for Hosted is to capture minimal metadata and token-level billing logs. Prompt text is redacted in logs by default for customers who request it; for Contracts we can add a clause to ensure prompt redaction/obfuscation. On Dedicated/Private we can provide stronger guarantees (no plaintext logs retained).

Next steps from Security Ops (Sean):
- Share canonical subprocessor CSV (attached) and a short mapping doc to show where data flows (Drive link).
- Prep answers to the vendor security questionnaire and pre-fill the vendor-security-questionnaire-template.xlsx for the top 10 checklist items.

Attachments: redwood_subprocessors_20261003.csv (stub), SOC2-TypeII-2025-Redwood.pdf (stub), vendor-security-questionnaire-template.xlsx (pre-filled stub)
